info.title: ChomikBox 2.0.8.2 network API (unofficial)
info.summary: Every network API used by the ChomikBox 2.0.8.2 Windows client of chomikuj.pl: the WCF SOAP service, upload/resume/download HTTP endpoints, web auto-login URLs, crash reporter and updater.
info.description:
Unofficial description of every network API used by **ChomikBox 2.0.8.2** (Windows desktop client of chomikuj.pl, Qt 4, released 2017-10-21), documented from the client's behaviour and verified against the production service on 2026-10-24. Open questions were then settled by a live follow-up on 2026-10-24/25. Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the live behaviour is documented and the difference is recorded in `x-discrepancies`.

<!-- variant:deviation -->
> **Non-conformance notice: per-operation view.** This document **intentionally deviates from OAS 3.2.1 §4.5.1** (Server Object `url`: "Query and fragment MUST NOT be part of this URL"). Each SOAP operation gets its own path item (`/Auth`, `/Folders`, …) by declaring the path-level server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so the concatenated URL becomes `…/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Auth`. The physical endpoint (`POST http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`) and the dispatch by `SOAPAction` are identical to the canonical document; WCF ignores the query. Tools that parse the server URL instead of concatenating strings may build `…svc/Auth?op=`, which fails. The deviation is declared in `x-oas-deviation`. **The strictly conformant document `chomikbox.openapi.yaml` (one `post` on the physical endpoint, `SOAPAction` enum, `oneOf` envelopes, `x-soap-operations`) is canonical**; it is generated from this file by `tools/build-strict.mjs`.
<!-- /variant:deviation -->

## Status and disclaimer

Unofficial documentation, not affiliated with or endorsed by chomikuj.pl or the ChomikBox authors. It grants no rights to the described service and no licence to its content (`info.license` is a `LicenseRef` stating exactly that). Test only against your own account and inside a dedicated sandbox folder: some server behaviours are destructive (see Security considerations S-03, S-04, S-05).

## API families

| Family | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SOAP service (18 operations) | `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc` | WCF, SOAP 1.1, no WSDL. 17 operations exist on the main service; SessionBegin targets a separate session host that no longer resolves. |
| Upload | `http://<server>/file/`, `/resume/check/` | Server, key and stamp come from UploadToken. Non-standard multipart framing. |
| File download | signed `http://sNNNN.chomikuj.pl/File.aspx?e=…&pv=…` | URL comes from Download/RefreshFileUrl. |
| Web pages | `http://box.chomikuj.pl/chomik/chomikbox/LoginFromBox?t=<token>&returnUrl=…` (307 to chomikuj.pl) and others | Opened in the browser; auto-login with the SOAP token. The public folder and file pages were probed anonymously (not client calls). |
| Telemetry | BoxEvents (SOAP), `http://bts.box.chomikuj.pl:8088/crash` | BoxEvents carries a fixed set of product events (verified live); the crash reporter is unverified. |
| Updater | `http://download.box.chomikuj.pl/updates` (default), `http://bts.box.chomikuj.pl/repo/…` | Not verified live; channel is dead (404/403). Packages are checked only against SHA-1 values from an unauthenticated `packages.xml` (C-07). |

<!-- variant:soap-conventions -->
## SOAP in OpenAPI: conventions of this per-operation view

**One path item per SOAP operation.** WCF dispatches on the `SOAPAction` header and ignores the query string, while a path suffix (`.svc/Auth`) fails with `a:DestinationUnreachable` and `.svc;Auth`-style matrix parameters redirect (302). Each operation therefore has its own path key (`/Auth`, `/Folders`, …) and a **path-item-level server** `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, giving `…/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Auth` (verified live: status `Ok`). This is the declared deviation above; the canonical document models the same operations as one `post` on the physical endpoint.

**Every SOAP operation** here is a `post` with a required `SOAPAction` header whose schema is `const` `http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/<Op>` (sent unquoted), media type `text/xml`, and the extensions `x-soap-action`, `x-verification`, `x-session`, `x-evidence` and, where relevant, `x-security-notes` and `x-discrepancies`.
<!-- /variant:soap-conventions -->

## SOAP wire format

Requests: `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`, always UTF-8) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/<Op>` (unquoted). Body: `<s:Envelope xmlns:s="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" s:encodingStyle="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/"><s:Body><Op xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…`, no SOAP header, no indentation, children unprefixed. **Parameter order matters**: WCF's DataContractSerializer reads forward only and silently drops an out-of-order parameter. Booleans: the client writes `0`/`1`, `true`/`false` work too. Request bodies may be gzip-compressed (`Content-Encoding: gzip`; the client does this). Service-level outcomes (including `BadToken` and `Error`) come with HTTP 200 and a `status` member; HTTP 500 carries a WCF SOAP fault.

**Default HTTP headers of the client.** ChomikBox itself sets only `Content-Type`, `SOAPAction` and `Content-Encoding: gzip` on SOAP requests. Qt 4.8.5 adds its defaults to every QNetworkAccessManager request that does not set them: `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0` (no product or version token), `Accept-Encoding: gzip` (replies are gunzipped transparently), `Accept-Language: <locale>,en,*` from the Windows locale (e.g. `pl-PL,en,*`; `en,*` for the C locale, `<name>,*` for `en-*` locales), `Connection: Keep-Alive` and `Host` (Observed for the Qt library, Inferred with high confidence for the client, which sets none of these itself). The SOAP captures send the same set (with `Accept-Language: en,*`). Exceptions: the music player's stream GET sends `Accept-Encoding: ` (a single space) to switch gzip off, and uploads over the default raw-socket transport (`[proto-box] direct-upload=true`) bypass the Qt HTTP stack, so these defaults presumably do not apply there (Inferred). crashsender.exe and the updater use the same Qt library (Inferred: same defaults).

**Namespaces.** All request members are in `http://chomikuj.pl/` (with trailing slash). Responses: `<OpResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><OpResult xmlns:a="http://chomikuj.pl" xmlns:i="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"><a:status>…`; nested struct members (FolderInfo, FileEntry, settings, …) are unprefixed, i.e. in `http://chomikuj.pl/`. **CheckEventsResult and AddFolderResult differ**: `a:` is `http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/TeamSolutions.Chomik.DAO.ChomikBox`, `status`/`errorMessage` redeclare `xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl"`, and `changes` children use `b:` = `…/TeamSolutions.Chomik.Library.DAO.ChomikBox`. The real client matches by local name only.

**XML modelling.** Schemas use the OAS 3.2 XML Object on every element: `xml.namespace` is always explicit (absent means "no namespace", as for SOAP fault children), `xml.prefix` records the prefix used on the wire (absent means unprefixed). Reusable content components (`FolderInfo`, `Token`, …) carry `xml.nodeType: none`, and the element name/namespace/prefix is declared at the point of use next to the `$ref` (OAS 3.2 §4.26.6.6 pattern). Lists are `type: array` with `xml.nodeType: element` (wrapper) and named items. `i:nil="true"` maps to `null` (nullable types). Attributes (`<resp res="1" fileid="…"/>`, `xml:lang`) use `nodeType: attribute`; mixed element+text uses `nodeType: text`. Property order equals wire order.

## Session model

There is no HTTP-level authentication. `Auth` returns a `token`, which the client sends as the first child `<token>` of every other SOAP request body (not expressible as an OpenAPI security scheme; see `x-session` and the `Token` schema). `status=BadToken` means the token is unknown or logged out; the client then re-runs Auth once and resends the message. Several tokens of one account are valid at the same time; Logout ends only its own token; no expiry was seen within ~45 minutes. The same token is passed as `t=` to the web auto-login URL (security scheme `boxToken`).

## Examples

Every captured case in `api/examples/<Dir>/<case>.*` appears as a named Example Object: 142 cases from the first live run and 85 from the follow-up of 2026-10-24/25, whose descriptions name the follow-up run. `serializedValue` holds the captured bytes **after redaction and, where noted, elision** (`Folders/root-depth2` has pre-existing folders elided and an XML comment inserted; see each example's description), or the body part of raw `.http` captures; `dataValue` holds the same data as parsed against the schema. The file is referenced with the extension **`x-externalValue`**, not `externalValue`: OAS 3.2.1 (§4.19.1) and its JSON Schema forbid `serializedValue` and `externalValue` in the same Example Object. `x-externalValue-part: body` marks a value that is the body of a raw HTTP capture; `x-capture-meta` points to the capture metadata (headers, sizes, timing, notes). Captures that have no body to show (GET requests, redirect responses) are kept as whole HTTP messages under `x-request-examples` (operation) and `x-response-examples` (response). Examples without a capture are labelled "Derived from client behaviour (not captured live)".

Captures are **redacted** with these placeholders: `{{COOKIE}}`, `{{EXISTING_FOLDER_NAME}}`, `{{FOLDER_PASSWORD}}`, `{{OTHER_PATH}}`, `{{OTHER_USER}}`, `{{PASS_HASH}}`, `{{RANDOM_PASS_HASH}}`, `{{SEED}}`, `{{SESSION_ID}}`, `{{SIGNED_E}}`, `{{SIGNED_PV}}`, `{{SIGNED_URL}}`, `{{STAMP}}`, `{{TOKEN}}`, `{{UPLOAD_TOKEN}}`, `{{USERNAME}}`, `{{WRONG_PASS_HASH}}`. `NOT-A-REAL-TOKEN` is a deliberately fake token. `sandbox-pass-123` (ModifyFolder examples) is a throw-away password the capture tool set on its own, since-deleted sandbox folder; it is not a secret. `{{OTHER_USER}}`/`{{OTHER_PATH}}` replace other users' account names and paths in the read-only foreign-file Download captures (file extensions kept). Numeric account/folder/file ids are real. The `Content-Length` values in raw captures refer to the unredacted bytes.

## Verification status

`x-verification` on every operation (also as badge tags): **verified-live** = request and response shapes confirmed against production; **partially-verified** = some parts not exercised live (named in the operation description); **unverified** = documented from the client's behaviour only, never exercised against the service. The badge `probe` marks operations the client never sends (live probes of unused URLs and of the endpoint's failure modes). `x-evidence` lists the example files behind each operation (paths relative to this file).

<!-- variant:summary -->
Current status (38 operations): 33 verified-live (23 client-facing + 10 probes), 5 unverified.
- probes (badge `probe`, never sent by the client): `getSettings` (a service operation the client never calls), `probeSessionPath`, `headFile`, `imageRedirect`, `musicFileLegacy`, `openPublicFolderPage`, `openPublicFilePage`, `loginFromBoxLegacy`, `soapRestStylePath`, `getServiceMetadataPage`
- unverified: `sessionBegin`, `sendCrashReport`, `getUpdateRepository`, `getUpdatesDirectory`, `openBetaRepository`
<!-- /variant:summary -->

## Security considerations

Summary of the security, privacy and robustness register; the full discussion is on the site page [Security](../site/security.html). Ratings are a coarse guide for readers of this documentation, not a formal assessment (High = exposes credentials or account control; Medium = exposes private data or can silently damage data; Low = information disclosure or hardening gap; Info = behaviour worth knowing). Affected operations carry the relevant entries in `x-security-notes`.

| ID | Rating | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| C-01 | High | All client traffic uses plain HTTP (SOAP, upload, resume check, downloads, web login hand-off, updater, crash reports). The SOAP service also answers on HTTPS, but the client never uses it. |
| C-02 | High | The login credential `passHash` is an unsalted MD5 of the password, sent in clear in every Auth: it is password-equivalent and cheap to crack. |
| C-03 | Medium | The same hash is stored in `conf.ini` (`[userinfo] password-hash`, plus proxy credentials), readable by any process running as the user. |
| C-04 | High | Crash reports upload `conf.ini` (with the password hash), `message.log`, both transfer queues, the playlist, chomikId and chomikName over plain HTTP to `bts.box.chomikuj.pl:8088`; the only integrity value is MD5 of `project-version.arch`. |
| C-05 | Low | Verbose logging by default (`message.log`), which then rides along in crash reports. |
| C-06 | Medium | The session token travels in clear in every SOAP body and as a URL query parameter (`LoginFromBox?t=`), where it becomes a full web session (`ChomikSession`) and can leak via logs, history and proxies. |
| C-07 | High (requires a network position) | Updates come over plain HTTP and are applied with administrator rights, protected only by an unauthenticated hash: each package is checked by SHA-1 against the `sha1` attribute of `packages.xml`, which comes over the same channel without any verification (no signature, no key; a mismatch is called "Signature error"), and `installer.exe` runs package commands without any prior check. Anyone who can alter the traffic (hostile network, DNS, proxy) can supply a matching manifest and package that runs elevated. The repository answered 404/403 on 2026-10-24, but a network attacker does not need the real server. |
| C-08 | Low | The single-instance named pipe and the `chomik://` scheme accept commands (`-d<url>`, `-u`, `-p`) from any local process or web link. The pipe also accepts `--file-server <host>`, which redirects all uploads and resume checks, upload keys included, to that host (command Observed; effect Inferred, the link to the upload path was not fully confirmed). |
| C-09 | Info | Usage data `stats{isUploading, isPlaying, isDownloading, panelSelectedTab, animation}` rides on every CheckEvents poll. BoxEvents is not off by default: it sends fixed events whenever they occur (`shutdown` = `poweroff`/`suspend`/`quit`, `detected.defaultplayer`, `settings.defaultplayer`, `settings.autostart`). |
| C-10 | Info | `base.ini` `key` and similar checks are integrity/tamper detection, not authentication. |
| C-11 | Info | Internal addresses are hard-coded in client components (e.g. RFC1918 `192.168.10.30` in chomikbox1conf.exe). |
| C-12 | Info | The NPAPI "Click Catcher" browser plug-in is obsolete; modern browsers no longer load it. |
| S-01 | Medium | Account enumeration via Auth: an unknown user gets `Forbidden`, a known user with a wrong password gets `PermissionError`. |
| S-02 | Medium | Folder passwords are returned in plain text over HTTP: ModifyFolder echoes the new password, Folders lists each folder's `password`, and the folder created by SavePlaylist gets a server-generated password while `passwd=false`. |
| S-03 | Medium (integrity) | A fault that does not roll back: MoveFolder with `newFolderId = folderId` returns `a:InternalServiceFault` (HTTP 500), but the folder has still been moved to the account root. |
| S-04 | Medium (data loss) | RemoveFolder `force=false` only protects folders that contain files; a folder holding only subfolders is deleted with all of them, status `Ok`. |
| S-05 | Low-Medium | Silent fallbacks instead of errors: Folders with an unknown folderId returns the root; MoveFolder to an unknown parent moves the folder to the root (`Ok`); UploadToken with an unknown folderId returns `Ok`. |
| S-06 | Low | Out-of-order or wrong-namespace parameters are silently dropped (null/0); some malformed requests (operation element without the trailing slash, the `hamsterId/folderId` Download id, an empty Auth) trigger an unhandled `a:InternalServiceFault`. The client's own "download folder" action builds exactly that `hamsterId/folderId` id, so that feature presumably fails against today's server (Inferred). |
| S-07 | Low | Contract disclosure through faults and headers: `a:DeserializationFailed` names parameters and CLR types, `a:DestinationUnreachable` leaks internal origin host names, and responses carry `x-powered-by: ASP.NET` and `x-server`. |
| S-08 | Low | Signed `File.aspx?e=…&pv=…` download URLs are reusable bearer URLs (repeat GET and Range work); `expire` was always empty, so their lifetime is unknown. |
| S-09 | Info | `Image.aspx?id=<fileId>` redirects anonymously to a signed URL (observed for an own PNG in a non-protected folder; file ids are sequential; protected folders untested). |
| S-10 | Info | Concurrent sessions are allowed; Logout invalidates only its own token; no expiry was observed within about 45 minutes. |
| S-11 | Info | The client identity is not enforced: Auth accepts any `ver` and works without the `client` element, so any program can present itself as ChomikBox. |
| S-12 | Low | `session.box.chomikuj.pl` (SessionBegin) no longer resolves in DNS; whoever registered it would receive the user name and password hash from old clients with `session-enabled=true` (off by default). |
| S-13 | Low (correctness) | Sequenced-Download state is per session, not per request: stored parts are keyed by the session token (not the stamp), are not cleared by a final part, and a stale part from another folder makes a later final part silently return an empty list (status `Ok`). Clients that reuse a session can get wrong or empty results. |
| S-14 | Info | ModifyFolder accepts `description`, `freePoints` and `freeTransfer` and silently ignores them: any in-range value (including -1, Int32.MaxValue and a 10,000-character description) returns `Ok` and moves `modifyTime`, but nothing is echoed, Folders never returns a value, and no effect was visible in download offers, public pages or the balance. The client never sends these fields. |

x-session.transport: SOAP body: <token> is the first child of every request except Auth and SessionBegin. No cookies, no HTTP auth, no SOAP header.
x-session.badTokenHandling: status=BadToken -> the client re-runs Auth (message-relog-count = 1 per message), replaces <token> in queued messages and resends them; messages flagged sessionBound are dropped. Messages flagged noRetransmit (Logout, CheckEvents) or noRelog (BoxEvents) are not retried.
x-session.concurrency: Multiple tokens of one account are valid concurrently; a new Auth does not invalidate earlier tokens (verified live).
x-session.lifetime: No expiry observed within ~45 minutes (not measured beyond).
x-session.timers: CheckEvents: one single-shot timer whose period is the shortest one currently requested: 300 s normally, 60 s while uploading, 15 s while a folder view is open (default values). Folders refresh every 300 s; SOAP reply timeout connection-timeout 20 s (clamped 5..120); pending-message validator every 5 s aborts messages older than 15 s (Download 45 s).
x-session.webSession: LoginFromBox?t=<token> converts the SOAP token into a web session cookie (ChomikSession).

x-discrepancies.live: Server has no `public` parameter and ignores it; the parameter is `publicUpload`. Server also accepts freePoints, freeTransfer, description and view{gallery}; the first three are accepted and ignored on every observable path, and the client never sends any of the four.
Only folderId (DAO datacontract namespace).
status and errorMessage only.
res and fileid only; errors carry errorMessage (res=-42 "Bad token").
res=-31 when nothing is stored or the key is unknown.
Refuses only folders containing files; folders with only subfolders are deleted.

/Auth.description: SOAP operation `Auth`. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on `SOAPAction` and ignores the `?op=/Auth` query.

servers.description: ChomikBoxService WCF endpoint; the trailing `?op=` turns the path key into an ignored query (`…svc?op=/Auth`).

post.summary: Log in and obtain a session token
post.description:
Authenticates with the account name and the MD5 of the password and returns the session `token` used by every other call.

**When the client sends it:** start-up auto-login, after system resume (`resume-login-delay`), and as the re-login triggered by `BadToken`.

**Outcomes (live):** `Ok` with hamsterId/name/token; unknown user gives `Forbidden`; wrong password gives `PermissionError` (both with every other member nil); an empty body triggers an unhandled server exception (`a:InternalServiceFault`, HTTP 500). Neither `ver` nor `client` is enforced. A new Auth does not invalidate earlier tokens.

**Client behaviour:** `Forbidden`/`PermissionError` open the credentials dialog; other errors schedule a delayed re-login (`delayed-login-interval`, Inferred 20 s). A reply arriving while already logged in is discarded.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Auth`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/Auth`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Auth` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

parameters.name: SOAPAction
parameters.description: WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (`SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Auth`); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give `a:ActionNotSupported`.

parameters.name: Content-Encoding
parameters.description: Present when the body is gzip-compressed (`[network] soap-use-gzip=true` in the default config; zlib level -1, windowBits 31). Accepted by the service (`Auth/success` vs `Auth/success-uncompressed-request`).

requestBody.description: SOAP 1.1 request envelope for `Auth` (media type `text/xml`, charset UTF-8).

success.description:
Captured live on 2026-10-24T15:25:09Z: `POST http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`.
Request: `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Auth`, `Content-Encoding: gzip` (249 bytes on the wire, 385 uncompressed; the example shows the uncompressed XML).

x-security-notes.text: All client traffic uses plain HTTP (SOAP, upload, resume check, downloads, web login hand-off, updater, crash reports). The SOAP service also answers on HTTPS, but the client never uses it.
The login credential `passHash` is an unsalted MD5 of the password, sent in clear in every Auth: it is password-equivalent and cheap to crack.

The session token travels in clear in every SOAP body and as a URL query parameter (`LoginFromBox?t=`), where it becomes a full web session (`ChomikSession`) and can leak via logs, history and proxies.
Account enumeration via Auth: an unknown user gets `Forbidden`, a known user with a wrong password gets `PermissionError`.
Concurrent sessions are allowed; Logout invalidates only its own token; no expiry was observed within about 45 minutes.
The client identity is not enforced: Auth accepts any `ver` and works without the `client` element, so any program can present itself as ChomikBox.

post.summary: End the session
post.description:
Invalidates the token it carries. Other tokens of the same account stay valid (`CheckEvents/first-session-after-other-logout`); a second Logout with the same token gives `BadToken`.

**When the client sends it:** on logout and when the system suspends; the local token is cleared first and the message is never retransmitted (`:noRetransmit`).

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Logout`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/Logout`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Logout` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

post.summary: Poll account state and change markers
post.description:
Periodic keep-alive/poll. Returns the current settings, the account balance and `changes/folderModifyTime`; when that tick count is newer than the local folder tree the client re-reads it with Folders(0,0). There is no event list: the `new` member was nil in every reply, including 15 probes right after uploads, ModifyFolder calls, SavePlaylist and folder removals (`after-upload`, `after-saveplaylist`), and the client never reads it (it looks up only `accountBalance`, `settings` and `changes`). Whether the server ever fills `new`: Unknown.

**When the client sends it:** right after a successful Auth, then on a single-shot timer whose period is the shortest one currently requested (default values): 300 s normally (`[proto-box] check-events-period`), 60 s while the uploader is busy (`check-events-uploading-period`), 15 s while a folder view is open (`check-events-folders-period`). Adding a shorter period sends CheckEvents at once. Session-bound and never retransmitted. After more than `check-events-repeat-count` (3) consecutive errors the client re-logs.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/CheckEvents`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/CheckEvents`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

post.summary: Read account settings
post.description:
Returns `settings{downloadByBox}`, the only member that exists. **The client never sends GetSettings** (nothing in the client invokes it). The client gets the same `settings` from every CheckEvents reply and writes `downloadByBox` to `[downloader] enabled` (shared with the handler of this reply). Verified live as a probe (`success`, `bad-token`).

**When the client sends it:** never (see above).

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/GetSettings`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/GetSettings`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/GetSettings` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

parameters.description: WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (`SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/GetSettings`); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give `a:ActionNotSupported`.

parameters.description: Present when the body is gzip-compressed (`[network] soap-use-gzip=true` in the default config; zlib level -1, windowBits 31). Accepted by the service (`Auth/success` vs `Auth/success-uncompressed-request`).

post.summary: Change account settings
post.description:
Writes `settings{downloadByBox}`, the only member. Live verification only wrote back the value just read (no actual change). A failure is only logged by the client ("SetSettings failed").

**When the client sends it:** the downloader module sends `SetSettings(downloadByBox = [downloader] enabled)` whenever it applies its configuration: at start-up and on every configuration change (Observed; exact timing Inferred). The opposite direction is CheckEvents, whose `settings/downloadByBox` is written back to `[downloader] enabled`, so the option "handle downloads with ChomikBox" is synchronised both ways.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/SetSettings`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/SetSettings`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SetSettings` (unquoted). post.summary: Read the folder tree
post.description:
Returns a folder and its subfolders down to `depth` levels (0 = unlimited). The client always asks for the whole tree from the root (`folderId=0, depth=0`) and rebuilds its model.

**Caveat (live):** an unknown `folderId` returns status `Ok` with the **root** folder; check the returned `id`. The full tree of a real account can be large (~212 KB for 586 nodes).

**`description`, `freePoints`, `freeTransfer`:** nil for every folder in every response, also right after ModifyFolder set them (`after-set-*`, `after-full-form-modify`, `price-probe-with-fields`) and for all 586 folders of the test account. **`Playlisty`** (created by SavePlaylist) has `passwd=true` and a server-generated password (`playlisty-after-duplicate`, redacted).

**When the client sends it:** after Auth (0,0); on the `refresh-folders-period` timer (300 s); when CheckEvents or a folder operation reports a newer modify time. Session-bound.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Folders`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/Folders`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Folders` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

post.summary: List the audio files of a folder (player)
post.description:
Lists the **audio** files of a folder for the music player as `<EntryInfo>` items (`id, name, type, size`). Only `disposition=player.audio` is accepted (`download` gives `WrongDisposition` even when audio is present, other strings `Error`). Folders without audio files, and unknown folders, give an empty `entryList`. For a listing of all files of a folder use Download with a folder path.

**Verification:** verified live with one 1-second silent MP3, and in the follow-up with a folder holding MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, M4A and WMA files, a subfolder and an `.m3u` playlist: the six audio files are listed, newest first, all with `type=file`; the subfolder and the `.m3u` are not listed, and an empty subfolder gives an empty `entryList` (`audio-folder-with-subfolder`, `subfolder-empty`). A playlist folder lists its copied files (`playlist-folder`).

**`type`:** only `file` has ever been seen, and the client handles only `file`: it compares the value case-sensitively and silently skips any other. Whether the server can send another value: Unknown.

**When the client sends it:** the file-selection window / player "add music files".

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/FolderFiles`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/FolderFiles`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/FolderFiles` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

parameters.description: WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (`SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/FolderFiles`); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give `a:ActionNotSupported`.

post.summary: Delete a folder
post.description:
Deletes a folder.

**Force semantics (live):** `force=false` refuses only folders that **contain files** (`NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder`); a folder that contains only subfolders is deleted together with them and status is `Ok`. `force=true` deletes files and subfolders. Unknown or already removed ids give `NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder` with `force=false`. **Caveat (exploration, not captured):** an already removed id with `force=true` returned `Ok`, so `Ok` does not prove that something was deleted.

**Client behaviour:** on `NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder` the client asks the user and may resend with `force=true`.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/RemoveFolder`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/RemoveFolder`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/RemoveFolder` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

parameters.name: SOAPAction
parameters.description: WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (`SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/RemoveFolder`); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give `a:ActionNotSupported`.

parameters.name: Content-Encoding
parameters.description: Present when the body is gzip-compressed (`[network] soap-use-gzip=true` in the default config; zlib level -1, windowBits 31). Accepted by the service (`Auth/success` vs `Auth/success-uncompressed-request`).

/ModifyFolder.description: SOAP operation `ModifyFolder`. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on `SOAPAction` and ignores the `?op=/ModifyFolder` query.

post.summary: Change folder properties
post.description:
Changes folder properties. **Verified live:** `name`, `password`, `hidden`, `adult`, `publicUpload` and `view.gallery` change and are echoed in `folderDetails`. Omitted or nil parameters are left unchanged. Returns the folder after the change and the tree modify times.

**`description`, `freePoints`, `freeTransfer`: accepted and ignored on every observable path** (exercised live on sandbox folders that were empty or held one 201-byte own file, each value reverted). Any in-range value returns `Ok` and moves `modifyTime` (each `prevModifyTime` equals the previous call's `modifyTime`): 0, 1, 100, -1, 1048576 and 2147483647 (Int32.MaxValue) for the two numbers; plain text, Polish letters with XML-escaped markup, an empty string and 10,000 characters for `description`. Nothing is echoed (`folderDetails` keeps the three members nil), Folders never returns a value (also seen from the parent), and there is no effect on the owner's Download offer (`own`/0 before and with the fields set), on the anonymous public folder and file pages (`openPublicFolderPage`, `openPublicFilePage`) or on the balance (checked after every step). A non-numeric or empty `freePoints`/`freeTransfer`, and a `freePoints` of 2147483648 (one above Int32.MaxValue; not tried for `freeTransfer`), give HTTP 500 `a:DeserializationFailed` naming the parameter and its type `System.Nullable<Int32>`, raised before the operation runs; no application-level error was ever returned for these members. Whether the server writes them to a store that no interface reads: Unknown.

**The client never sends them**: its folder-options dialog has widgets for a description, free transfer (in MB) and free points, but they are hidden. Their meaning is Inferred from those widgets and the client's folder tooltip "This folder has %1 of free transfer.": transfer (kB) or points the folder owner sponsors for downloads, not a price.

The password `sandbox-pass-123` in the examples is a throw-away value the capture tool set on its own sandbox folder (deleted afterwards), not a real folder password.

**Client vs server (live):** the 2.0.8.2 client sends its last flag as `<public>`, which the server does not know and silently ignores; the server parameter is `publicUpload`. The password is echoed back in plain text.

**When the client sends it:** folder options dialog (`FolderOptions`); only changed fields among `name`, `password`, `hidden`, `adult` and `public` are sent.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/ModifyFolder`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/ModifyFolder`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/ModifyFolder` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

parameters.name: SOAPAction
parameters.description: WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (`SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/ModifyFolder`); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give `a:ActionNotSupported`.

parameters.name: Content-Encoding
parameters.description: Present when the body is gzip-compressed (`[network] soap-use-gzip=true` in the default config; zlib level -1, windowBits 31). Accepted by the service (`Auth/success` vs `Auth/success-uncompressed-request`).

/Download.description: SOAP operation `Download`. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on `SOAPAction` and ignores the `?op=/Download` query.

servers.description: ChomikBoxService WCF endpoint; the trailing `?op=` turns the path key into an ignored query (`…svc?op=/Download`).

post.summary: Resolve files and agreements; obtain signed download URLs
post.description:
Resolves download entries to files, lists the agreements (transfer types) offered for each file, and, once an agreement is accepted, returns a signed `url` for `GET /File.aspx`.

**Two steps (as the client does):** (1) send entries without `agreementInfo`: each FileEntry lists the offered agreements and `url` is nil; (2) resend with the accepted agreement: `url` is filled. For own files the only offer is `own`/cost 0 (balance unchanged); paid agreements were never accepted live.

**Agreements offered (live):** exactly one per file in every case seen: `own`/0 for own files; `small`/0 for other users' files under 1 MB; `transfer` with cost = file size in kB, rounded down, above 1 MB (1654 for a 1,694,208-byte file). The foreign-file captures are read-only: nothing was accepted. `free`, `edu`, `access` and `points` were not observed. The 7 `agreementInfo` slots follow the client's type order: the offered name sits at its type's position (Observed: own in slot 1, small in 2, transfer in 6; Inferred for the others) and the other slots are nil. `AgreementInfo` lists every name the client knows and the cost units.

**Outcomes by disposition:** `download` works for any file. `player.audio` works like `download` for audio files (agreement offer first, then a signed url: `mp3-audio-disposition-request`, `mp3-audio-disposition-own-agreement`). For other files it returns `Error` / `failed : requested file(s) not available` with `list` and `accountBalance` nil (`audio-disposition`).

**Forms:** plain (`token, disposition, list`) or sequenced (with `sequence{stamp, part, count}`). The client uses the sequenced form and splits a request only above 2000 entries, so its normal requests are single messages (count 1). **Ids:** numeric file id; file path `/<user>/<folder>/<file>`; folder path `/<user>/<folder>` (returns all files of the folder, also for other users' folders: `foreign-folder-listing-offers`). `.<realId>` is accepted (status `Ok`) but has never been shown to resolve a file: `realId` was nil or 0 for every file seen (own uploads, playlist copies, other users' files), so only an unknown realId could be tried. The client builds `.<realId>` only for entries without a file id. The client's `<hamsterId>/<folderId>` form, built by its "download folder" action, triggers an unhandled server exception (`a:InternalServiceFault`), so that client feature presumably fails today (Inferred).

**Sequenced Download: verified live with conditions** (26 exchanges in four sessions, own files only):
- A non-final part (`part < count-1`, a middle part included) is acknowledged with status `Ok`, `list` and `accountBalance` nil and `messageSequence` echoed. Its entries are stored server-side **per session token**: a second, concurrent session of the same account gets `Error` for the final part (`seq1d-*`).
- The store is **not keyed by the stamp and not cleared** by a final part; a new part 0 replaces what was stored (`seq1c-c4-final-d`, `seq1c-c5-final-alone-c`, `sequence-final-part-without-part0`).
- A final part returns the stored entries plus its own, resolved and grouped as usual, **only if they are all in one folder**; it does not expand the folder (`sequence-final-part1-of-2`, `seq1c-c2-final-d`, `seq1c-c4-final-d`).
- If the combined entries span **two folders**, the reply is `Ok` with an **empty** `<a:list/>` (balance present): nothing is returned, not even the final part's own entry, and a stale stored part from another folder also empties a later final part (`sequence-final-after-part0-other-folder`, `sequence-count3-final-part2`, `sequence-final-part-alone-own-agreement`).
- A final part with **nothing stored** in the session gives status `Error` with a nil `errorMessage` and nil `list` (three sessions: `sequence-final-part-alone-fresh-session`, `seq1c-c0-final-alone-fresh-session`, `seq1d-session2-final-d-same-stamp`).
- **Agreements count only in the final message:** with `own` in the final part both entries got a `url`; with `own` only in part 0 neither did (`sequence-own-agreement-final-part1-of-2`, `seq1c-c9-final-d-no-agreement`). Whether a final-message agreement applies per entry or per type: Unknown.
- A count-1 message ignores stored parts (`single-message-after-sequences`). The balance was unchanged throughout.

Consequences (Inferred): a client request of more than 2000 files from more than one folder would come back empty, and two sequenced requests running in one session (downloader and player) could mix their parts (S-13).

**When the client sends it:** downloader and player; `:resentTimeout` = `message-download-resent-timeout` (45 s). Download results that contain files set a `guid` tracking cookie.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Download`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/Download`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Download` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

parameters.name: SOAPAction
parameters.description: WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (`SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Download`); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give `a:ActionNotSupported`.

Signed `File.aspx?e=…&pv=…` download URLs are reusable bearer URLs (repeat GET and Range work); `expire` was always empty, so their lifetime is unknown.

Sequenced-Download state is per session, not per request: stored parts are keyed by the session token (not the stamp), are not cleared by a final part, and a stale part from another folder makes a later final part silently return an empty list (status `Ok`). post.summary: Obtain an upload ticket (key, stamp, server)
post.description:
Issues an upload ticket for one file: `key`, `stamp`, the upload `server` (`host:port`, varies per call) and `locale`. The client then posts the file to `http://<server>/file/` (see `uploadFile`) or, for an interrupted upload, first asks `GET /resume/check/`.

**Live:** the folder id is not validated when the ticket is issued.

**When the client sends it:** uploader start, and again after a failed resume. Session-bound.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/UploadToken`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc`; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (`.svc/UploadToken`) does **not** work (`a:DestinationUnreachable`, see `soapRestStylePath`).

**Wire format.** `POST` with `Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8` (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers `text/xml; charset=utf-8`) and `SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/UploadToken` (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (`Content-Encoding: gzip`).

post.summary: Get a fresh signed URL for an expired download link
post.description:
Returns a new signed `url` for a file whose link expired. Works for own files without a prior agreement in the session; unknown ids give `Ok` with `url` nil. `expire` was nil in every reply (whether the server ever fills it: Unknown). The reply echoes `id`; `realId` came back as `0` for a playlist copy whether `0` or `-1` was sent, so the realId sent is ignored when the id is valid.

**`expire` in the client:** parsed only from this reply, only when non-empty, and only in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` (local time; a Unix time, an ISO `T`, fractions or a zone suffix leave the previous value). It serves only the warning shown when the user pauses downloads ("%n file(s) are going to expire…", threshold `[downloader] warn-before-expire` in seconds: application default 3600, default config 60); as implemented the comparison computes now - expire, which looks inverted (Inferred bug). There is no proactive refresh: an expired link is detected when the HTTP download fails.

**When the client sends it:** when a download link has expired; session-bound.

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/RefreshFileUrl`. post.summary: Save a player playlist as a folder in the account
post.description:
Saves the player's playlist to the account. **A playlist is an ordinary folder** named after the playlist, created inside a top-level folder `Playlisty`, which the server creates at the account root when missing (`parentId` is its id). There is no parent parameter. The listed files are **copied** into the playlist folder under new file ids (`Download/playlist-folder-listing`). The playlist folder came back with a server-generated `password` value while `passwd=false` (`Folders/playlist-folder`). It is removed like any folder (`RemoveFolder/playlist-folder-force`).

**Verification:** verified live in the real-client form (`token, name, list`, unused id = -1) in guarded runs with full-tree snapshots. An existing `Playlisty` is **reused** (same `parentId`), and a duplicate playlist name becomes a new folder `<name>(1)` (no space) with status `Ok` and a fresh copy of the files (`duplicate-name-playlisty-exists`, `Download/playlist-duplicate-listing`). `Playlisty` itself has `passwd=true` and a server-generated password (`Folders/playlisty-after-duplicate`, redacted).

**When the client sends it:** player "save playlist to hamster".

**Routing.** The path item declares the server `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=`, so this operation resolves to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/SavePlaylist`. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the `SOAPAction` header (verified live). After a successful Auth, and only if `[proto-webox] session-enabled=true` (default **false**), the client posts this SOAP message (SOAPAction `http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SessionBegin`, gzip disabled for this message) to `http://<session host>/session`, where the session host is `[proto-webox] webservice-session` or `session.box.` + domain. The client reads nothing from the reply.

**Live status:** not verifiable. The main service does not implement SessionBegin (`a:ActionNotSupported`, see `soapEndpoint` example `main-endpoint-not-supported`), `session.box.chomikuj.pl` has no DNS record, and `http://box.chomikuj.pl/session` redirects to an error page (`probeSessionPath`). No credentials were sent to any session host. Both examples below are derived from the client's behaviour.

post.summary: Upload a file (non-standard multipart)
post.description:
Stores one file using an UploadToken ticket.

**URL.** The client first builds `http://<server>/file/?key=..&stamp=..&folderId=..&fileName=..[&imageSize=WxH][&locale=..]` and then posts to `scheme://host/path`, i.e. **without the query** (the server does not need it).

**Body.** `Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=!CHB<stamp>` with the client's own part framing (see `UploadMultipartBody`): parts `chomik_id`, `folder_id`, `key`, `time`, [`resume_from`], [thumbnail parts], `client`, `locale`, `file`. With the exact client framing the stored file is byte-identical (verified by SHA-256 after download).

**Transport.** With `[proto-box] direct-upload=true` (default) the client uses a raw socket (`POST <path> HTTP/1.0`, `Host`, `Content-Length`); otherwise QNetworkAccessManager. Captures used HTTP/1.1 with Content-Length; no difference observed. Network errors are retried (`send-retry-count` 5; delay `[network] send-retry-delay`, application default 15 s, clamped 1..300 s; the INI line `upload-retry-delay = 15` is not read).

**Headers.** Besides `Content-Type` and `Content-Length` ChomikBox sets no header. Over the default raw-socket transport the Qt 4.8.5 defaults (`User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0`, …) presumably do not apply (Inferred); over QNetworkAccessManager they do (see "SOAP wire format" in `info.description`).

**Forced file server.** The start-up switch or single-instance pipe command `--file-server <host>` makes the client post every upload, upload key included, and every resume check to that host instead of the UploadToken `server` (effect Inferred, C-08).

**Generators beware.** The part header lines are fixed (see `UploadMultipartBody` `x-part-headers`): text parts `name="…"` + `Content-Type: text/plain`, thumbnails `Content-Type: image/jpeg`, and the `file` part **only** `name="file"; filename="…"` with **no Content-Type**. A default OpenAPI multipart serialiser (Content-Disposition, Content-Type per part) corrupts the stored file.

**Reply.** XML `<resp res="1" fileid="…"/>` served as `text/html`; `res != 1` is an error with `errorMessage`.

get.summary: Ask how much of an upload is already stored
get.description:
Before resuming an interrupted upload the client asks the upload server how many bytes are stored for the ticket `key` (flags `:noRelog`, `:sessionBound`). The server is the forced file server (`--file-server <host>`, start-up switch or pipe command; C-08) or the UploadToken `server`. Headers: the Qt 4.8.5 defaults (Inferred, see "SOAP wire format").

**Client logic:** `res=1` and 0 < `file_size` <= local size: resume with `resume_from=file_size` (thumbnails only if `skipThumbnails="false"`); `file_size` > local size: restart with a new UploadToken; `res=-4`: network error; other errors: new UploadToken. **Live:** `res=-31` before any byte is stored and for unknown keys.

get.summary: Download file bytes (also used for audio streaming)
get.description:
Plain GET of the signed URL. The client resumes and splits downloads with `Range: bytes=N-M` / `bytes=N-` and parses `Content-Range: bytes N-M/T`; the default config allows one connection per file (`max-connection-count = 1`). An expired link triggers RefreshFileUrl. The URL is reusable (several GETs worked). **Headers:** the downloader's GET carries `Range` when resuming or splitting, plus the Qt 4.8.5 defaults `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0`, `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, `Accept-Language: <locale>,en,*` and `Connection: Keep-Alive` (Inferred for this request).

**Player streaming**: the player GETs the `player.audio` URL with `Icy-MetaData: 1`, `Accept-Encoding: ` (a single space, disabling Qt's gzip) and optionally `Range: bytes=N-`; it requires HTTP 2xx, Content-Length > 0 and no `x-nofile` header, and treats a redirect to `/File.aspx` as failure.

get.summary: Open the web site logged in with the session token
get.description:
The client opens web pages in the browser through this auto-login URL (`[proto-webox] web-box-service-url`, chomikuj.pl brand overlay `http://%1/chomik/chomikbox/LoginFromBox?t=%2&returnUrl=/`, with `%1` = the service host `box.chomikuj.pl` and `%2` = the raw Auth token). The client's first request therefore goes to `http://box.chomikuj.pl/chomik/chomikbox/LoginFromBox…`, which redirects once (307) to the same URL on `chomikuj.pl` (`loginfrombox-box-host`). There the service sets a web session cookie (`ChomikSession`) and redirects to `returnUrl`.

**Pages opened this way** (the other `web-box-*` templates append to this URL, so the page lands in `returnUrl`): `web-box-info-url` = `/ChomikBox` (generic default `/Box`), `web-box-add-transfer-url` = `/DodatkowyTransfer.aspx` (generic `/AddTransfer.aspx`), `web-box-add-points-url` = `/DodatkowePunkty.aspx` (generic `/AddPoint.aspx`), `web-box-freedback-url` (sic) = `/ChomikBoxOpinia.aspx` (generic `/BoxOpinion.aspx`), `web-box-user-url` = `/<user>`. The captures used the generic page names; only the redirect was recorded, no page was followed and nothing was bought.

**Invalid token:** 302 to `/` without `ChomikSession`. The client builds `%1/t=invalid&returnUrl=` on logout.

get.description:
Public web page of a folder: `http://chomikuj.pl` followed by the folder path, i.e. the same string as the folder's `DownloadFolder/globalId` (`/<account>/<folder>/<subfolder>`; Observed for the captured folders). Only status and headers were recorded; the body digest is kept in each capture.

post.description:
Not verified live. After a crash the Breakpad handler of chomikbox.exe starts `crashsender.exe [--no-gui] chomikbox 2.0.8.2 win32 <dump> <message.log> <conf.ini> <uploadQueue.ini> <downloadQueue.ini> <playlist> <hamsterId> <hamsterName>`; argv[3], the architecture, is the constant `win32`. Unless `--no-gui` is given the user is asked first. crashsender POSTs `multipart/form-data` (see `CrashReportBody`) with QNetworkAccessManager; no custom headers besides Content-Type (Qt 4.8.5 adds its defaults, Inferred).

**Reply handling (Observed):** the reply body, the HTTP status and the headers are never read; only `QNetworkReply::error()` is checked. On an error the GUI mode shows a box "Error occured" with "Error: <error string>" (only logged with qDebug under `--no-gui`); there is no success message and **no retry**, and the process always quits after the first reply or error. Qt 4.8 maps HTTP 4xx/5xx to errors, so any 2xx (and an unfollowed 3xx) counts as success whatever the body says (Inferred). The server's behaviour is Unknown: no report was sent.

**Privacy:** the report includes `conf.ini` (login, password MD5, proxy credentials) and `message.log`.

get.description:
Not verified live; the channel is dead (404/403). **URLs**: with `[repository] dist` empty (the default config value) the base is `http://download.box.<domain>/updates` (`getUpdatesDirectory`); with a non-empty `dist` (stable, testing, unstable, …) it is `http://bts.box.<domain>/repo/dists`. Every file URL is `<base>[/<dist>][/<arch>]/<name>` (`arch` = `[repository] arch`, application default `win32`), or the repository URL after a `Location` redirect ("repository redirect"). The check runs every `[repository] updater-period` minutes (1440).

**Flow** (Observed client behaviour, never exercised):
1. `packages.xml` (root `upackages`; `package` elements with `file` children carrying `name`, `sha1`, `size`, `gzSize`, `privileges`, `updater`, `exec` and other flags, plus `symlink`, `status`, per-brand `domain`, `changelog`, `release`) is downloaded and parsed **without any hash or signature check**. File names are guarded against paths outside the repository.
2. Installed files whose SHA-1 already matches are skipped.
3. Each needed file is fetched as `<url>.gz` when it is gzipped (falling back to the plain file), staged in `<tmp>/chomikbox.tmp/`, and the SHA-1 of its (decompressed) content is compared with the `sha1` attribute. A mismatch, including an empty `sha1`, is error 3, shown as "Signature error". There is no signature and no embedded key: the client uses only a SHA-1 hash.
4. The package entry with `updater="exec"` and `privileges="admin"` (a client constant; `any` never matches) is started through the Windows `ShellExecute` call with verb `runas` when the staged exe's manifest requires administrator (`installer.exe`), otherwise `open` (`installeru.exe`, asInvoker). Which updater a repository nominates is repository data (Unknown).
5. `installer.exe` executes the work list (copy, link, remove, run command) without any hash, signature or size check. Its only content check is a post-copy SHA-1 of the installed files that decides whether the package is marked `installed` (no rollback, no error). The SHA-1 of the work list passed as argv[2] is not checked (Inferred, medium-high confidence).

Plain HTTP; ChomikBox sets no headers, Qt 4.8.5 adds its defaults (Inferred). See C-07.
